title: Break-Even Calculator
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Entrepreneurship
description: Sliders for Price per Sale, Cost per Sale, Fixed Monthly Costs and Sales This Month drive a live break-even calculation: sales needed = Fixed Monthly Costs / (Price per Sale - Cost per Sale), rounded up to a whole sale. A result card shows the division with the current numbers, and a bar shows sales this month against the break-even line, red below it and green at or above it, with the month's profit or loss. A price at or below the cost per sale shows a warning instead of a number. Defaults are Jordan's $40 price, $8 cost per sale and $120 fixed monthly costs.

prerequisites: Chapter 14 reading through Projecting Revenue and Finding Break-Even
Basic arithmetic: subtraction, division, and rounding
educational.topic: Break-even thinking: how price, cost per sale and fixed monthly costs set the number of sales a lean venture needs each month
learningObjectives: Calculate the number of sales needed to break even from price, cost per sale and fixed monthly costs
Explain why a fractional break-even result rounds up to the next whole sale
Predict how the break-even number changes when price, cost per sale or fixed monthly costs change
Recognize that a price at or below the cost per sale can never break even

controls.label: Price per Sale
controls.purpose: Set what one customer pays for one sale

controls.label: Cost per Sale
controls.purpose: Set what it costs to deliver one sale

controls.label: Fixed Monthly Costs
controls.purpose: Set the costs the venture pays each month regardless of how much it sells

controls.label: Sales This Month
controls.purpose: Set this month's sales; the bar turns green once it reaches the break-even number

controls.label: Load Jordan's Numbers
controls.purpose: Set Price per Sale to $40, Cost per Sale to $8, Fixed Monthly Costs to $120 and Sales This Month to 5

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Calculator practice with immediate feedback: the worked division, the rounding step and a red/green bar update on every slider change
keyQuestions: How much does each sale leave over to pay the fixed costs?
Why does a break-even result of 3.75 mean 4 sales, not 3?
Which change lowers the break-even number more: raising the price by $8 or cutting the cost per sale by $8?
What happens to break-even when the price falls to the cost per sale?
commonMisconceptions: Break-even is fixed costs divided by price, forgetting to subtract the cost per sale
A fractional break-even result can be rounded down
Selling more always fixes a loss, even when each sale costs more than it brings in
assessmentOpportunities: Calculate a break-even number by hand before checking it on the result card
Predict the direction of change in break-even before moving a slider
Calculate the break-even number for one's own venture idea and judge whether it is realistic
